title: I’m making a bluffing card game with AI assistance. Lose a round, lose a finger.
author: Paper_Lynx
selftext:
**Hey!**   
  
I’m a solo developer working on **9 Fingers**, a dark card game made in Unity.

You play cards face down, lie about their value and decide when to call someone’s bluff. There’s cash to win, but every round you lose costs you a finger.

You can face the boss solo or play online with up to three players plus the boss. Everyone is competing against each other. You can also peek at cards with a mirror, mark them with a razor or steal someone’s bonuses. Friendships should be perfectly safe :)

I use Codex as part of my workflow, and there’s been a lot of testing, feedback and iteration along the way. One thing I’ve learned is how specific that feedback needs to be. “Make this better” gets you much less useful results than pointing out exactly what feels wrong and explaining why.

I’m happy with how the game is coming together, so I wanted to share some gameplay here. Happy to talk about the process too.

Anyone else here working on a Unity game with AI assistance? What still takes the most manual work for you?

Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4311910/9\_Fingers/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4311910/9_Fingers/)
